lines.text: חמן 325 חמץ
16. Impers. חַם לוֹ, fut. יֵחַם לוֹ, it is
warm to him, he is made warm, gets
warmth, 1 K. 1, 1. Ecc. 4, 11.—Trop. of
the mind as heated, excited, Ps. 39, 4;
and so of heat from wine Jer. 51, 39;
from lust Hos. 7, 7. Also of cattle, to be
in heat, to conceive, Gen. 30, 38. 39; see
in יָחַם.—Inf. חֹם, c. suff. בְּחֻמָּם Jer. 51,
39. Once חֲמַם, with pref. in pause
לַחְמָם for warming sc. oneself, Is. 47, 14.
Niph. part. plur. נֵחָמִים, burning, in-
flamed, sc. with lust, c. בְּ Is. 57, 5.
Piel to warm, to make warm, Job 39,
Hithp. to warm oneself, Job 31, 20.
Deriv. חָם II, חֹם, חַמָּה, חַמָּן, and the
proper names חַמּוּאֵל, חַמּוֹן, חַמַּת.
חַמָּן, only in plur. חַמָּנִים, images, idols
of some kind for idolatrous worship, Lev.
4. 34, 7; in which passages it is several
times joined with statues of Astarte,
אֲשֵׁרִים; while from 2 Chr. 34, 4 it ap-
pears further that the חַמָּנִים stood upon
the altars of Baal. Arabs Erpen. and
Kimchi long ago explained the word by
suns, images of the sun; and both this
interpretation and the thing itself are
now clearly illustrated by ten Punic
cippi with inscriptions, consecrated to
בעל חמן (בעל כמן) i. e. to Baal the solar,
Baal the sun. See the subject fully
treated in Thesaur. p. 489. Monumm.
Phœnic. p. 170 sq.—The form חַמָּן solar
is from חַמָּה the sun; and the plur.
חַמָּנִים in the O. T. is put ellipt. for
בְּעָלִים חַמָּנִים, and is found in the same
context as elsewhere בְּעָלִים.
* חָמַס fut. יַחְמֹס 1. to do violence
to any one, to oppress, to wrong; pr. to
be eager, vehement, and hence violent,
i. q. חָמֵץ no. 3. a. Arab. حَمِسَ in a
good sense, to be active, brave, con-
stant, حَمَاسَةٌ warlike valour; comp.
שָׁדַד. Jer. 22, 3. Prov. 8, 36 he that sin-
neth against me, חֹמֵס נַפְשׁוֹ wrongeth his
own soul, injures himself. Job 21, 27
מְזִמּוֹת עָלַי תַּחְמֹסוּ the plans wherewith ye
think to oppress me, how ye may over-
come me. חָמַס תּוֹרָה to violate a law
2. to tear away with violence, e. g. a
hedge, Lam. 2, 6. Also to tear off from
oneself, i. q. to shake off; Job 15, 33
יַחְמֹס כַּגֶּפֶן בִּסְרוֹ like a vine he shall
shake off his unripe grapes.
NIPH. to be treated with violence, Jer.
13, 22; i. e. by impl. to be violently made
bare, as the other clause shows.
Deriv. תַּחְמָס, and
חָמָס m. 1. violence,oppression,wrong,
49. Prov. 3, 31, and אִישׁ חֲמָסִים 2 Sam.
22, 49. Ps. 140, 2. 5, a violent man, op-
pressor. עֵד חָמָס a wrongful witness,
i. e. false, Ex. 23, 1.—A genitive or suffix
after this word may refer either to him
who does the wrong, or to him who
suffers it. Of the former kind are חֲמָסוֹ
his wrong i. e. which he does, Ps. 7, 17,
חֲמַס יְדֵיכֶם 58, 3, comp. Ez. 12, 19. Of
the latter, חֲמָסִי my wrong i. e. done to
me Gen. 16, 5, חֲמַס בְּנֵי יְהוּדָה Joel 4, 19;
also Judg. 9, 24. Obad. 10. Hab. 2, 8. 17.
Jer. 51, 35. So Lat. injuria, e. g. Cæs.
Bell. Gall. 1. 30 ‘ pro veteribus Helveti-
orum injuriis populi Romani,’ i. e. done
to the Roman people; see the Commen-
tators, and comp. Heinrich ad Cic. part.
inedit. p. 21.
2. Meton. what is got by wrong, ill-
gotten wealth, Am. 3, 10. Plur. id. Prov.
* חָמֵץ fut. יֶחְמַץ, inf. חָמְצָה Hos. 7,
4, to be sharp, pungent.
1. As to taste, to be sour, acid, leav-
ened, e. g. fermented or leavened bread
Ex. 12, 39. Hos. 7, 4; or vinegar, see חֹמֶץ.
Also to be salted, seasoned, see חָמִיץ.—
Arab. حَمُضَ, Syr. ܚܡܰܥ.
2. As to sight, colour, to be bright,
splendid, so as to dazzle the eyes;
spoken espec. of a bright red or scarlet
colour. Part. pass. חָמוּץ splendid, gor-
geous, spoken of the scarlet mantle or
pallium of a prince, Is. 63, 1; comp. אָדֹם
v. 2, and Sept. Syr.—In the same manner
the Greeks say χρῶμα ὀξύ i. e. κόκκινον,
πορφύραι ὀξύταται, ὀξυφεγγῆ ῤόδα, see
Bochart Hieroz. I. p. 114. Simonis Arc.
Formarum p. 66, 102.
3. Trop. of the mind: a) to be eager,
vehement; to do violence, like kindr.
חָמַס; whence part. חֹמֵץ a violent man,
oppressor, Ps. 71, 4. Comp. חָמוֹץ and

line_status.note: The left header word has only three letters (ח, מ, and a final letter with a plain straight descender = final nun ן); there is no yod between mem and the final letter, and the descender lacks the final-kaf form, so Reading B's חמיך is wrong. The right word is clearly חמץ (final tsade with hooked tail). Sequence matches the lexicon order חמן … חמץ.

Printed left-to-right order: immediately after "names" comes חַמּוּאֵל, then חַמּוֹן, with חַמַּת rightmost before the period — Reading B's order. Reading A reverses the list. Pointing (patach + dagesh in mem, shureq in חַמּוּאֵל, holem in חַמּוֹן) is identical in both and matches the print.

First word begins with ב (dagesh + sheva, with the bottom-right heel of beth, not the open foot of pe) followed by ע with qamets; the type is בְּעָלִים "Baals", not פְּסִלִים — consistent with Gesenius' point that חַמָּנִים are sun-images of Baal and with the same word בְּעָלִים recurring at the end of the next line.

The second Hebrew letter is an open ע with a qamets beneath (not a closed round ס), and the first letter is ב with sheva+dagesh, not פ; the same word בְּעָלִים is printed in line 2 ("for בְּעָלִים חַמָּנִים") and fits Gesenius's Baal connection (2 Chr 34:4). No dot pattern matching פְּסִלִים is present.
The Arabic verb is printed حَمِسَ with a kasra clearly visible beneath the mīm (not a fatḥa above it), so Reading B's vocalisation is correct; the wider gap before "Arab." is also as printed.
The stem label is printed in small capitals (large N, small-cap I P H), not mixed-case "Niph."; the remainder of the line is identical in both readings.

The commas after "violence" and "oppression" are set tight with no following space (the line is crowded to the right margin); the Hebrew חָמָס with two qamets and final samekh is identical in both readings.
Printed form is defective חֹמֵץ: holem dot sits directly over the heh with no vav between heh and mem (three letters only: ח מ ץ). Reading B's plene חוֹמֵץ is not what is printed.
